summary: The Assumptions page now offers three quick choices for stock growth (careful 6%, middle 7%, hopeful 8%) and for prices rising (2.5%, 3%, 4%), with what forecasters expect beside them. After you save, it tells you what the change did to your retirement answer, for example that the money now runs out at 69 instead of 70.
points: A growth figure above 8% shows an amber warning that it is higher than any forecast we know
Will the money last? shows a before and after line for your change
A hopeful return gets an amber tag so a higher number never reads as a fix
numbers: Runs out at 69 instead of 70 in the example

summary: On Retirement contributions, each 401(k) row now asks when you want to pay the tax: later, now, or some of each. If you split it, the page shows how much this year's federal tax changes (about $190 in the example) and how your money will be mixed at retirement between pay-later, already taxed and regular savings.
points: Some of each saves two rows and keeps the whole employer match on the pay-later one
Rule of thumb in plain words, plus the 2026 rule for catch-up money for pay over $150,000
Paycheck and Work benefits now count both rows
Saving no longer lands a few cents over the yearly limit
numbers: $190 less federal tax in the example

summary: The document reader now understands a pasted pay stub: it shows your 401(k), your Roth 401(k) and the employer match apart, each as a proposal you accept with Use it. A 401(k) you never typed in gets filled in or created for you, and numbers already on file are marked so nothing is changed twice.
points: Works on the phone with no AI and no PC, from pasted text
Asks how often you are paid when the stub does not say
Account numbers are never read or kept
A Roth line is no longer mistaken for before-tax money

summary: Import now reads the Quicken or QuickBooks download that most banks offer next to CSV, right on the phone with no column step. It picks your account, skips lines it already has if you load the same file twice, and can set the account balance to the bank's own figure.
points: Only the last 4 digits are shown, never saved
Works for older and newer bank file styles and odd text encodings
Card charges keep their sign like the rest of the plan
The page no longer mentions Plaid, whose free tier ended

summary: The work board notes that the retirement request landed and its claim was released.
One builder claimed the next three retirement engine parts (L9 to L11) on the team board.

In Get started, if you say you work but leave the pay box empty, the page now shows a gray typical-pay figure for your age and state and saves it, marked as our guess. Typing your own figure ends the guess, and saying you are retired or not working removes it.
points: Based on census pay data for full-time workers, smoothed by age
The next question says when the guess moved to your age
numbers: 135 lines of new checks on the page
